title: The deferred 3D chunk (three + graph-3d.ts) is ~88% of its 150 KB gzip ceiling: bumping three or importing more of it can fail test:bundle
body: scripts/bundle-budget.check.ts caps the deferred chunk at `DEFERRED_BUDGET_KB = 150` (gzip). The built dist/_astro/graph-3d.*.js measured ~131.6 KB gzip on 2026-10-29 (129.8 KB on 2026-08-25), so there is under 20 KB of headroom. A `three` version bump, one more three class (e.g. a new geometry, loader, or material), or a heavy dependency pulled into graph-3d.ts can push it over. The ceiling exists to make that an explicit decision, not to forbid it: measure after `pnpm run build` with `pnpm run test:bundle`, and if going over is justified, raise the constant in the same diff with the reason. Do not dodge it by splitting three across chunks or by static-importing pieces into the critical path (that breaks the separate critical-JS budget, 4 KB).
not_derivable: The check knows the ceiling, not the current size; how close the chunk already is only appears after a build.

evidence.summary: gzip of dist/_astro/graph-3d.DuPzAgjJ.js = 134,725 bytes (~131.6 KB) measured 2026-10-29 on branch spike/landing-v2.
